design: L231 does the LEFT-heavy Perron mode have a SOURCE? L216's unregistered finding is that the anatomical operator's dominant mode is strongly left-heavy on every beta pool cell (A_inf +0.26 to +0.44, pct_abs 1.000). This card asks it NONSELECTIVELY (Kriegeskorte step 1): the SAME per-cell-mean asymmetry of v1 over five cord pool pairs, every super_class, and the whole labelled population, on four cord operator arms plus a whole-graph arm, with BH-FDR across the entire family instead of a percentile on a preselected pool. The reconstruction caveat is the table's first two rows: per-side cell COUNT and per-side in-mass.

cert_gen.note: generic machinery certified on f4wA BEFORE any new substrate was built (L44).

cert_gap.note: L210 ran this on the GAIN-SCALED operator; the L216 beta operator is the same operator up to the scalar g_f4wA and a spectral RATIO is invariant to a global rescaling (L209's no-op law)

gain_invariance.note: R is gain invariant; the cross-substrate comparison is therefore admissible without re-bisecting a gain per substrate.

side_census.note: BANC v626 reconstructs one optic lobe far more completely than the other; the whole labelled population is right-heavy 2.0:1 in CELL COUNT while the ventral nerve cord, where L216's finding lives, is balanced to 0.96. Declared in PREREG 0a-2 as OBSERVED before registration.

whole_graph_arm.note: PREREG 0e: accepted only on the RESIDUAL, with the four certified cord arms printed as the calibration reference. Beta only (PREREG 0d).

P1.registered: A_glob > 0 on the primary arm (cord subnet's whole labelled population is LEFT-heavy in per-cell Perron overlap)

P3.registered: at least 3 of 5 pools BH-significant on the primary arm
P3.status: PARTIALLY OBSERVED (Ti/Tr under a DIFFERENT null, PREREG 0g)

P4.registered: whole-graph NATIVE all-population A_v1 < 0 (RIGHT-heavy), given the 2.0:1 right-heavy cell count and the 8.4:1 optic-lobe imbalance

P5.registered: |rho(A_v1, A_count)| < 0.70 on the primary arm (F_CONFOUND does not fire)

P6.registered: at least one super_class BH-significant with |A| >= 0.10 on the primary arm

limitations: (1) The whole-graph arm is BETA only (PREREG 0d) — the Crofts reweighting is constructed inside the certified SUBS loop and was not re-implemented outside it. (2) The restricted units are keep_wA-intersected on every arm (PREREG 0c) so arms are compared on identical cell sets; one extra Pr_bL cell that exists unrestricted is in no unit. (3) The union null is NOT L216's within-group null (PREREG 0g); both are reported for Ti/Tr. (4) The whole labelled population's side census is right-heavy 2.0:1 in CELL COUNT, driven 8.4:1 by the optic lobe, so any whole-graph asymmetry is confounded with reconstruction completeness BY CONSTRUCTION — which is why the branch rests on the cord subnet, whose count ratio is 0.96. (5) p-values for the large units rest on 5000 sampled draws (floor 1.9996e-04); the small units are EXACT. (6) A_inmass is measured in the ARM's OWN operator currency, so on the Crofts arms it is the degree-reweighted mass, not raw |log1p(syn)*sign|; the primary arm is beta, where it is the raw ladder mass with BETA_L on inhibitory edges. (7) The branch's sign leg compares np.sign of two measured reals; both are far from zero on the primary arm, and the signed median pool value is stored beside it so a near-zero case would be visible.
